paths.description: Public desktop QR-linking entry point; represents the unauthenticated shell.
Public linking entry at 360x800; represents narrow-screen reflow.
Keyboard focus probe across all visible public actions.
Chat list, conversation, composer, search, settings, media/calls and account management; not covered because a real linked account is required.

findings.summary: The public login surface does not follow the system dark-theme preference.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots captured with default media and prefers-color-scheme: dark are visually identical light surfaces, despite dark tokens existing elsewhere in the CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply the existing dark token set to the unauthenticated login root and declare color-scheme so browser UI and all login surfaces follow the system preference.

findings.summary: The login card is clipped and unusable at a 360 px viewport.
findings.evidence: The 360x800 screenshot cuts off the QR code, heading, instructions and footer horizontally. The document hides overflow, so layout metrics report no scrollbar while content is still inaccessible.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the fixed 780 px login composition with intrinsic, fluid sizing and a single-column narrow layout; do not hide overflow as a substitute for reflow.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated and several actions expose very small visual targets.
findings.evidence: The focus probe focused each visible role=button control and computed outline:none and box-shadow:none. Visible action boxes were only 16-20 px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic anchors/buttons, provide a clear :focus-visible ring, and expand each action hit area to at least 24x24 CSS px, preferably 44x44 for touch.

findings.summary: The lightweight login screen paints slowly.
findings.evidence: The trace measured FCP 2.99 s and LCP 5.96 s; Lighthouse measured FCP/LCP 8.1 s and a 0.58 performance score.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the login shell separately from the authenticated application and render its critical content before loading chat-only code.

findings.summary: The login route ships the authenticated application bundle before it is needed.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 6.38 MB transferred, including 5.81 MB of JavaScript across 27 requests; Lighthouse estimated 940 KiB unused JavaScript and 161 KiB unused CSS. Several parser-inserted resources are high-priority render-blocking candidates.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a minimal login entry bundle, code-split authenticated features behind successful linking, and defer non-critical scripts and styles.

findings.summary: The login document lacks semantic headings and uses generic div controls.
findings.evidence: DOM/evaluate probes found no h1-h3 elements and no anchors; all visible actions are div role=button. Combined with absent visible focus, this weakens structural navigation even though Lighthouse automated accessibility scored 100.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark “Scan to log in” as the page h1 and use native a/button elements for actions, retaining accessible names and keyboard behavior.

findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported one deprecated API warning, a BFCache blocker, a missing/late charset declaration and an unsized image audit failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the deprecated API and BFCache blocker, move a UTF-8 meta charset into the first 1024 bytes, and reserve dimensions for the flagged image.

findings.summary: A Referrer-Policy header is absent from a security-sensitive application.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirmed HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff, CSP frame-ancestors and Permissions-Policy, but no Referrer-Policy header. The CSP also permits unsafe-inline for styles.
findings.suggestedFix: Send an explicit strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter Referrer-Policy, and continue reducing CSP unsafe-inline where feasible.

findings.summary: Resource use is disproportionate to the unauthenticated login task.
findings.evidence: The public linking screen transfers 6.38 MB, 98.5% from static.whatsapp.net, before an account is linked; 5.81 MB is script.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the unauthenticated shell within a route-specific budget and fetch authenticated features only after successful linking.

findings.summary: The initial login surface has a very large JavaScript heap footprint for its visible complexity.
findings.evidence: A post-load heap summary reported 1,314,301 heap nodes and 74,935,444 bytes self size while the rendered DOM probe counted 323 elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the unauthenticated entry point, avoid instantiating authenticated stores/workers before linking, and set a bounded heap budget for the login shell.
